summary: Automated priority inference loop causing cascading reroutes and duplicate escalation labels in routing templates
description:
Issue summary:
Automated priority inference service (enrichment-service v2.6.0) is intermittently adding duplicate escalation labels and triggering cascading reroutes across the support routing templates. The duplication causes tickets to be routed to multiple escalation queues and creates artificially inflated SLA escalations in reporting.

Impact:
- Internal routing churn: a single incoming ticket gets duplicated routing bindings across two escalation tracks for ~5-12 minutes before de-dup resolves.
- Alert noise: SLA breach dashboards show spurious increases for P1 cohorts (up to +8 percentage points) during run windows.
- Potential customer-impact risk if real escalations are delayed by misrouted duplicates.

Environment:
- prod | us-east
- Affected services: enrichment-service (priority inference), template-indexer, routing-engine, analytics pipeline.
- Observed after a template-indexer deployment on 2026-03-11 (indexer v4.1.0).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Inbound ticket passes through enrichment-service which computes priority and suggested labels.
2) Template-indexer receives enrichment output and applies template bindings.
3) Routing-engine expands bindings and creates route assignments.
4) In some runs, enrichment emits both `escalation:team-alpha` and `escalation:team-alpha_v2` transiently for same ticket id due to race between TTL refresh and ancestry merge.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate escalation labels for same ticket ID persisted in routing-engine for ~5-12m until the template dedupe job runs.
- Analytics shows duplicate increments in per-route SLA counters.
- Manual fixes (support unassign + reassign) temporarily resolve.

Expected behavior:
- Enrichment should emit a single canonical escalation label per inference cycle. Template-indexer should dedupe overlapping bindings deterministically. Routing-engine should ignore near-duplicate bindings within the configured merge window.

Notes on urgency:
Given the P1 severity and visible SLA noise for internal dashboards used in escalations, this needs immediate mitigation while we implement a root-cause fix.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Initial triage by Support; observed correlation with template-indexer deploy on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC.
Hypothesis A: indexer v4.1.0 changed template update ordering causing ancestry key to be written twice during a short window.
Hypothesis B: enrichment-service v2.6.0 regression in TTL refresh produced two labels: canonical and _v2 alias; merge logic treats them as distinct until dedupe cron runs.

Query used: SELECT ticket_id, array_agg(distinct escalation_label) FROM routing_bindings WHERE created_ts > '2026-03-11T23:30:00Z' GROUP BY ticket_id HAVING count(distinct escalation_label) > 1 LIMIT 50; returned 342 hits in us-east.
Relevant logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/routing-engine/2026-03-12/streams.log lines 4821-4875 show duplicate bind writes for ticket id SUP-9987-xyz.

Dashboards: Kibana -> routing_engine_bindings (time window 2026-03-11T23:30 to 2026-03-12T10:00) link: https://kibana.redwood-internal/products/routing/bindings?from=2026-03-11T23:30&to=2026-03-12T10:00
Repro attempts in staging: template-indexer v4.1.0 + enrichment-service v2.6.0 combo reproduced dedupe gap but with smaller volume (approx 3-4 duplicates per 1k tickets).
Configuration snippet: template-indexer config `dedupe_window_ms` currently set to 300000 (5m). Suspect window too long or misapplied naming normalization.
Telemetry gap: routing telemetry pipeline counts unique route assignments after dedupe step; upstream duplicates will still inflate pre-dedupe dashboards causing noisy alerts.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Samir Patel (Routing Eng): Confirmed reproduction in staging. Hypothesis leans toward indexer ordering regression. Will try a rollback of indexer to v4.0.7 in prod canary tomorrow morning during low traffic window.

2026-03-12 15:14 - Priya Rao (SRE): Scheduling rollback window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Will monitor routing binding write rate and SLA counters. Alerting suppression requested for the noisy SLA metric during the rollback window (ops-alerts #suppression).

2026-03-13 02:25 - Samir Patel (Routing Eng): Rolled back template-indexer to v4.0.7 in us-east canary. Early signs: duplicate rate dropped by ~85% in canary. Proceeding to full rollout of rollback across us-east.
2026-03-13 05:50 - Diego Marquez (Product): Noted this surfaced in customer-facing dashboards briefly; need follow-up to ensure no regression on template semantics after rollback.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Samir Patel (Routing Eng): Root cause identified: template-indexer normalization change in v4.1.0 introduced aliasing behavior for some legacy template IDs; enrichment-service TTL refresh concurrently emitted both alias and canonical labels. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/template-indexer/pull/412. Work items: patch indexer + tighten routing-engine merge window + add post-apply dedupe check in analytics pipeline.

2026-03-14 11:03 - Elena Park (Support): Marking follow-up tasks: add unit test for alias normalization, add alert to detect >1 escalation labels per ticket post-enrichment, and update runbook. Assigning to Samir for fix and to Priya for deployment plan.
next_steps: Merge and deploy template-indexer patch PR 412 that restores deterministic normalization (owner: Samir).
Add a temporary routing-engine guard to ignore duplicate escalation labels that differ only by legacy alias suffixes (owner: Samir, timeline: 24h).
Shorten `dedupe_window_ms` from 300000 to 60000 for canary to reduce time window of duplicate persistence while patch stabilizes (owner: Priya, timeline: ASAP).
Add telemetry check: alert if >0.5% of tickets in a 1h window have >1 escalation_label emitted post-enrichment (owner: Analytics team, ticket for follow-up INT-174215).
Update runbook and add example queries and S3 artifact locations (owner: Support docs).
resolution: TBD - rollback performed as mitigation; awaiting template-indexer patch and routing-engine guard deployments. Will update after patch rollout and 72h observation window.
